title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 12 (Registered Office of Company)

content.overview: Section 12 requires every company to have a registered office capable of receiving and acknowledging all communications and notices, to file verification of the office, to paint or affix its name and address, and to notify any change of registered office in the prescribed manner.
content.glance: State the duty to have a registered office; note verification filing; list name-display and change-of-office requirements.
content.study: A company must have a registered office capable of receiving and acknowledging all communications and notices. Verification of the registered office must be filed with the Registrar. The company must paint or affix its name and the address of its registered office outside every office or place of business, and print its name and registered-office address on prescribed documents. Change of registered office within the same city or outside, including change of State, follows prescribed resolution and approval routes with filing of the altered memorandum where required. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in s. 12 and link to s. 10A verification and s. 13 alteration where the State changes.

sections.heading: Duty to Have a Registered Office
sections.body: Every company must have a registered office capable of receiving and acknowledging communications and notices.

sections.heading: Verification Filing
sections.body: Verification of the registered office must be filed with the Registrar within the prescribed time.

sections.heading: Name and Address Display
sections.body: Name and registered-office address must be painted or affixed outside offices and printed on prescribed documents.

sections.heading: Change of Registered Office
sections.body: Change within or outside local limits, and change of State, follow prescribed resolution and approval routes with filing.

examples.title: No registered office
examples.body: A company has no address capable of receiving notices. Section 12 is breached.

examples.title: Change of State
examples.body: A company shifts its registered office from one State to another. Special resolution and prescribed approvals plus filing of the altered memorandum are needed.

hypotheticals.question: Must the registered office be a place where the company actually carries on business?
hypotheticals.analysis: It must be capable of receiving and acknowledging communications and notices; it is the official address for service.

hypotheticals.question: What if the company changes its registered office without filing?
hypotheticals.analysis: Non-compliance with the filing and approval requirements under s. 12 is a statutory breach.

distinctions.title: Registered office vs place of business
distinctions.left: Official address for service and statutory communications
distinctions.right: Any location where business is carried on

misconceptions.trap: A company need not maintain a registered office after incorporation.
misconceptions.correction: Section 12 requires a registered office at all times after the prescribed period from incorporation.

misconceptions.trap: Change of registered office never needs approval.
misconceptions.correction: Change of State and certain other shifts require prescribed resolutions and approvals.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 12 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State the duty to have a registered office. II. Check verification and display. III. Analyse any change of office and required approvals. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Current office status; verification filing; display compliance; change procedure if any; precise relief.
